title: standardize-retry-priority-and-frame-errors-for-openai-shim
author: Priya Kothari
description:
Motivation: Clients implementing OpenAI-compatible semantics (rate limits, retry-after, idempotency) observed inconsistent retry behavior across hosted and dedicated backends. This caused duplicated tool/function calls and variable backoff behavior for streaming clients when mid-stream transient errors occurred. This PR standardizes retry semantics exposed by the Redwood API and the OpenAI compatibility shim, and strengthens structured error frames for streaming so that clients can make deterministic retry and deduplication decisions.

What this PR does (single-string summary): Adds a small, explicit 'retry contract' surface to errors and streaming frames, introduces a Retry-After-Priority header to disambiguate clock vs quota windows, formalizes Idempotency-TTL semantics returned to clients, and updates the OpenAI shim to map legacy headers into the new structured fields. Also includes integration tests, docs, and SDK compatibility notes.

Key changes (high-level):
- Response error shape now includes: code (string), message (string), retryable (boolean), retry_after_seconds (integer, null if not applicable), quota_bucket (string, for cardinality-based rate windows). These are surfaced for HTTP 429/503/504 and streaming error frames.
- New header 'Retry-After-Priority' with values 'clock' | 'quota' | 'server' to indicate the semantics of Retry-After when present. This allows clients to choose backoff strategies (e.g., clock-based sleep vs jittered retry).
- Idempotency TTL: server adds 'Idempotency-TTL' (seconds) in both success and error responses when an Idempotency-Key was provided, clarifying how long the server will hold deduplication state.
- Streaming frames: error frames are now JSON objects with fields {"error": {<structured error>}, "terminal": true|false}. Non-terminal streaming errors include retryable flag so the client can decide to continue or abort. Terminal=true indicates the stream should be considered closed by the server.
- OpenAI shim mappings: old headers (X-RateLimit-Reset, Retry-After) are translated into retry_after_seconds + Retry-After-Priority and quota_bucket; existing OpenAI-compatible flakey clients will still receive the normal OpenAI headers for backward compatibility but are encouraged to read the structured body.
- Backcompat shim: an optional compatibility mode (env REDWOOD_COMPAT_OLD_RETRIES=yes) writes legacy headers only; disabled by default in new deployments.

Commits (summary):
- Add structured error fields and tests (author: pkothari)
- Implement Retry-After-Priority header and mapping layer
- Streaming: implement structured error frames and update frame serializer
- OpenAI shim: map legacy headers into structured error payloads and add compatibility toggle
- Docs: API contract section, SDK guidance, migration notes
- Integration tests and CI fixes

Files changed (representative, small snippets included where useful):
- redwood/openai/shim/response_mapper.go: add toStructuredError(err) -> returns code/message/retryable/retry_after_seconds/quota_bucket and header mapping (snippet: 'resp.Headers.Set("Retry-After-Priority", priority)')
- redwood/runtime/stream/stream_serializer.go: replace plain-error-frame with structured JSON frames (snippet: 'frame.Data = json.Marshal(struct{Error interface{} `json:\"error\"`; Terminal bool `json:\"terminal\"`}{...})')
- redwood/api/http/headers.go: introduce constants for Retry-After-Priority and Idempotency-TTL
- redwood/tests/integration/retry_contract_test.go: new table-driven tests covering clock vs quota windows and idempotency TTL checks
- docs/api/retry-contract.md: adds examples, client pseudo-code for streaming and non-streaming flows
- redwood/observability/metrics.go: add metric rwd.retry_priority_emitted{priority} to monitor server-side decisions

Notes on compatibility and rollout:
- Backward compatible by default: we keep existing OpenAI headers but prefer structured body fields. SDKs will be updated in follow-up PRs to prefer structured fields first and fall back to headers.
- Feature flagging: the new header and structured frames are gated behind an opt-in config so that we can enable progressively across regions. The PR includes a migration playbook in docs/migrations/retry_contract.md.

Testing:
- Unit tests for mapping logic and serializer (run: make test ./...; all pass)
- Integration tests simulate quota windows and clock-based rate resets; we add a mock clock to deterministically exercise Retry-After-Priority decisions.
- Manual staging run: streaming clients (Node + Python) exercised 1k short lived streams with induced 429/503s. No duplicated tool calls observed when idempotency keys were used.

Operational considerations:
- Metric added to help detect misconfigurations when servers emit 'quota' but clients assume 'clock'.
- Logs include a short reason string when Retry-After-Priority is chosen (e.g. 'quota-window', 'global-quota', 'node-overloaded').
- Rolling enablement recommended: start with non-critical regions and enable compat mode for legacy integrations.

Related: ENG-2104 (retry contract design), ENG-2201 (stream framing for errors).

review_thread: Alejandro Ruiz (reviewer): Please add a short justification for choosing header + body shape vs only body. Clients often rely on headers for proxies—make sure the shim preserves both.
Priya Kothari (author): Added backcompat behavior to keep legacy headers by default; documented rationale in docs/migrations/retry_contract.md.
Meera Patel (reviewer): Integration tests look good. Is there a plan to limit the cardinality of quota_bucket? We should avoid unbounded cardinality causing metrics cardinality explosions.
Priya Kothari (author): quota_bucket is intentionally coarse (e.g., 'user:global', 'org:region') — clarified in code comments and added a unit test that asserts max 32 distinct buckets in a test run.
Liam O'Connor (reviewer): Streaming changes are significant; can we provide an opt-out for existing streaming SDKs in case of unexpected deserialization errors?
Priya Kothari (author): Added feature flag REDWOOD_COMPAT_OLD_RETRIES for streaming to emit old plain-string frames; off by default. Also added SDK guidance to catch structured frames defensively.
Alejandro Ruiz (reviewer): CI integration flake noted; reran tests after fix. Approving now.
Meera Patel (reviewer): Approve after adding one more comment on docs wording.

release_notes:
- Standardized structured error responses with retry metadata for HTTP and streaming.
- New Retry-After-Priority header to disambiguate retry semantics.
- Idempotency-TTL header added to clarify deduplication window.
- Streaming frames now include structured error objects with terminal flags.
- Backcompat mode available via REDWOOD_COMPAT_OLD_RETRIES.
See docs/api/retry-contract.md for migration steps.
